deferred_proposals.example: An arterial PO2 at or below 55 mm Hg, or an arterial oxygen saturation at or below 88%, taken at rest, breathing room air.
deferred_proposals.note: Numeric coverage criteria (PO2 cutoffs, SpO2 cutoffs, hematocrit threshold, percentage-change thresholds). Evaluation criteria, fail the claim-readability test -- logged for SME review. 2026-05-29 NCD 240.2.1 enrichment: 240.2.1 adds the 'middle band' (PO2 56-65 mmHg, SpO2 >=89%) covered conditionally on clinical-trial enrollment, complementary to 240.2's qualifying band (PO2 <=55, SpO2 <=88%). Together they map the policy threshold space for home oxygen.
deferred_proposals.resolution: Resolved 2026-06-05, Session 40 (20-policy checkpoint). Numeric coverage criteria (arterial PO2 / SpO2 thresholds at rest, during sleep, during exercise; hematocrit cutoffs; percentage-drop thresholds; LPM titration values; and similar threshold values across the home-oxygen, PAP, and respiratory-care policies) are evaluation criteria that fail the claim-readability test (SKILL.md §Extraction Taxonomy): the matcher does not see threshold values — a claim carries codes, modifiers, diagnoses, and dates of service, not numeric measurement values from clinical notes. Underlying domain content is already captured in the graph as gem:ClinicalConcept individuals naming the measurements themselves (arterial blood gas study, oxygen saturation, hematocrit) and the qualifying conditions (at rest, during sleep, during exercise, chronic stable state); the specific threshold values and compound disjunctive logic are preserved in policy gem:description text. The project's current mission is matching, not evaluation. Schema promotion deferred per Session 40 strategic call (Frame X confirmed): revisit when (a) the evaluation team requests structured evaluation criteria for downstream consumption, or (b) a comprehensive policy-reprocessing pass makes uniform schema additions cheap. See SKILL.md §Extraction Taxonomy (claim-readability test) and the Session 40 checkpoint report.

Currently the Group 1 N/A entry yields no code-level extraction, but the policy-level rule that 'only the listed codes support medical necessity' is a stronger statement than the per-code triples alone capture. A52492 (10 ICD covers — single Group 1) needs source verification before promotion. deferred_proposals.example: On claims for the first through third months, suppliers must add a KX modifier to codes for PAP equipment (E0470 or E0601) and accessories only if all of the criteria... have been met.
deferred_proposals.note: A52467 specifies elaborate KX/GA/GZ usage rules tied to specific code+condition combinations. SKILL.md mentions code-plus-modifier composite entities as a deferred category. The pattern is already in scope for the checkpoint review. A52492 (2026-05-31): AU-modifier scope-restriction rule — 'For this policy, codes A4450, A4452 and A5120 are the only codes for which the AU modifier may be used.' Different shape from KX-criteria-met or KO/KP/KQ unit-dose rules: a code-set scoping rule limiting which codes can carry a given modifier within the policy's domain. A52514 (S36 pass 5): the DNS-section qualifier 'For all claims submitted with the N3 modifier.' over a 5-ICD list (J96.01, J96.11, J96.21, J96.91, R09.02) is the conditional-EXCLUSION polarity of this pattern -- the ICDs are excluded only when the N3 modifier appears on the claim. Earlier instances (A52467 KX-criteria-met, A52492 AU code-set scoping) all expressed conditional-INCLUSION shapes. The eventual schema solution must handle both polarities.
deferred_proposals.resolution: Resolved 2026-06-05, Session 40 (20-policy checkpoint). Code-plus-modifier composite usage rules — the policy-stated rules governing which modifiers may, must, or must not be used with which HCPCS codes — pass the structural form of the claim-readability test (a claim DOES carry HCPCS+modifier combinations on line items), but they do not change matcher behavior under the project's current R1 matching contract (a claim matches a policy when the policy independently declares the code AND independently declares the modifier; the SELECTIVE rule governing whether the combination is valid is evaluator-territory). EMPIRICAL FINDING (worth preserving for the future-promotion pass): Selective applicability is the DOMINANT pattern in CMS modifier prose, not an exception. Examples surveyed at this checkpoint — A52466 (Nebulizers, 8 modifiers): JW/JZ (drug-wastage) selective to drug claims; KO/KP/KQ (unit-dose dispensing) selective to unit-dose drug codes with explicit J2545 / J7620 / Q4074 exclusions; KX selective to nebulizer/drugs/supplies/accessories; GA/GZ selective to KX-eligible codes when criteria not met. A52492 (Tracheostomy, 1 modifier): AU restricted to exactly 3 of 18 covered codes (A4450, A4452, A5120) by explicit policy statement. L33797 and A52514 (Oxygen, 14-16 modifiers each): N1/N2/N3 oxygen flow rate groupings and Q* oxygen test result indicators bind to specific oxygen equipment code subsets, not full code lists. The current structure (independent gem:coversProcedure and gem:refersToHCPCSmodifier lists, plus prose in gem:description) is INTENTIONALLY under-specified — the selective rules ARE present in source-policy prose but are not yet encoded as first-class structured data. DESIGN PROPOSAL FOR THE FUTURE PROMOTION PASS (Tom, Session 40): a lightweight gem:modifierRule datatype property on the policy, multi-valued, carrying one source-language statement of a selective-applicability rule per value. Schematic examples: gemi:a52492 gem:modifierRule "For this policy, codes A4450, A4452 and A5120 are the only codes for which the AU modifier may be used." . gemi:a52466 gem:modifierRule "Whenever a unit dose form code is billed, it must have a KO, KP or KQ modifier. (Exception: The KO, KP and KQ modifiers should not be used with code J7620.)" . This captures the rule TEXT for downstream evaluator consumption without committing to relation-level structural modeling (no gem:CodeWithModifier class, no gem:ModifierUsageRule individuals, no separate gem:appliesToCode / gem:requiresModifier / gem:relation predicates). The evaluation team can parse the rule text themselves or request structural promotion when their requirements are clearer. Cheaper than full schema promotion; cleaner than structured-language-in-description because the rules become queryable as their own predicate. Schema promotion deferred per Session 40 strategic call (Frame X confirmed): revisit when (a) the evaluation team requests structured code-modifier rules for downstream consumption, or (b) a comprehensive policy-reprocessing pass makes uniform schema additions cheap. At that time, the gem:modifierRule text property is the proposed starting point. See SKILL.md §Extraction Taxonomy (claim-readability test) and the Session 40 checkpoint report.

The matching value under Frame X / R1 contract is technically evaluator-territory (a claim line carries the modifier; whether the modifier is the CORRECT modifier given coverage-criteria status is evaluator logic), but the cost of capturing the vocabulary-level semantics is so low and the documentary value so high that promotion was approved at this checkpoint. deferred_proposals.concept_group: Audit script robustness to handoff template drift
deferred_proposals.example: S64 handoff §1 table changed column order from 'Lines | Bytes' (S57+ convention the parser was built for) to 'Bytes | Lines'. The parser's hard-coded 'second numeric column is Bytes' rule grabbed the Lines value as the expected byte count, producing 10 spurious RED hash_verify findings at S65 bootstrap. MD5 anchors matched (content was intact), but the size column comparison was apples-to-oranges. The 'halt on RED' bootstrap rule triggered against a content-correct file set.
deferred_proposals.note: Logged 2026-06-17 (Session 65 bootstrap). gem_audit.py's parse_handoff_table assumes column position; Option B (header-aware parser, implemented in S65) directly resolves this instance by reading the §1 header row and identifying Bytes/Lines columns by name. Broader principle: the audit script should distinguish 'spurious RED from template drift' from 'genuine RED from content mismatch.' Possible further hardening, beyond Option B's header-aware parsing: (a) magnitude heuristic as fallback when header inspection is inconclusive; (b) explicit 'template_drift' finding category, surfaced as YELLOW rather than RED so a future drift incident does not halt bootstrap on a content-correct file set; (c) verify Lines as well as Bytes (currently only one numeric column is checked, so a Lines mismatch with a Bytes match would pass silently). Cross-references: SKILL.md session bootstrap protocol; the 'halt on RED for reconciliation (excepting expected post-handoff hash mismatches where Tom directs proceed)' rule in userMemories.
deferred_proposals.resolution: Resolved 2026-06-18, Session 67 (20-policy checkpoint Cycle 2). Option B (header-aware parser) implemented in S65 directly addresses the root cause: gem_audit.py parse_handoff_table (lines 145-200) reads the §1 header row to identify Bytes/Lines columns by name, with the legacy position-based rule as fallback if header detection fails -- a two-layer defense. The three proposed further hardening sub-options offer marginal additional protection: (a) magnitude heuristic is redundant under Option B's two layers (would trigger only if both fail to disambiguate, a doubly-hypothetical scenario); (b) template_drift YELLOW category is speculative -- Option B prevents the original incident, and a future drift that bypasses Option B would inform the category design better than designing it preemptively (consistent with the 'no forward references to undesigned future work' principle from S66 §3); (c) Lines verification is redundant under MD5, since matching MD5 implies matching LF count by content identity. Cross-references: SKILL.md session bootstrap protocol; S65 §4.6 sub-option enumeration; S66 §3 'no forward references' principle; the 'halt on RED for reconciliation' rule in userMemories.

Added gem:CMSpolicyShape (33 sh:property blocks covering 26 single-domain CMSpolicy predicates + 6 union-domain predicates shared with AnchoredCodingScope + ruleDescription as datatype-only on the CMSpolicy branch) and gem:AnchoredCodingScopeShape (10 sh:property blocks: 3 single-domain appliesWhen* sub-properties + 6 union-domain duplicates + ruleDescription). Scope decision (S78 Borderline #1): cover only the GEM-extraction-relevant surface (CMSpolicy + AnchoredCodingScope); BaseServiceLine claim-data, EditResponse/EditResult pipeline, CoverageOutcome/CoverageRestriction/CoverageExclusion consumer-side, ServiceLine/MedicareClaim, RBCS healthcareService namespace, and owl:Thing/owl:Class schema-internal domains are out of scope and recorded as a new logged entry ("Extend SHACL coverage beyond GEM-extraction surface"). Value-class enforcement decision (S78 Borderline #4 -- surfaced after a first-Generate verification failure): two strategies are used by predicate-range kind. In-namespace gem: ranges (gem:ProviderCredential, gem:ClinicalConcept, gem:BenefitCategory, gem:CMSpolicy, gem:PolicyRule, gem:PolicyGroup, gem:PolicyCodingRule, gem:AnchoredCodingScope, gem:NextPlannedStep, gem:QualificationGroup) use sh:class -- typing triples are in GEM_ontology.ttl and visible to the merged validation graph. deferred_proposals.concept_group: SHACL invocation pattern: data_graph must include ontology for sh:class checks
deferred_proposals.example: During S73 Cycle 1 post-Generate verification, a standalone `pyshacl.validate(data_graph=instances_file, shacl_graph=ontology_file)` returned 50 spurious sh:class violations against gem:PolicyRuleShape -- every gem:ruleDomain_<value> and gem:ruleType_<value> was reported as 'not a gem:RuleDomain/gem:RuleType individual', even though those typing triples exist in GEM_ontology.ttl (e.g., 'gem:ruleDomain_screening a gem:RuleDomain'). Does NOT affect gem_audit.py, which uses hand-written rdflib queries against a graph that already merges both files; matters for future GraphDB validation pipelines, CI hooks, or developer-side validation. Pairs with deferred_proposals[75] (SHACL coverage scan for relationship predicates) -- when #75 lands, the invocation pattern should be documented in the same Generate so the new shapes are actually exercisable. deferred_proposals.concept_group: Policy status vocabulary (active / retired-in-place / retired-and-removed / never-determined)
deferred_proposals.example: NCD 200.2 (never retired), NCD 180.2 and NCD 240.2.2 (retired in place, section retitled RETIRED, isInEffect=true) and NCD 280.13 (retired 2012-06-08 and incorporated into NCD 160.27, section gone, isInEffect=false) all carry operatively identical 'no NCD is appropriate' content but three different provenances, distinguishable only by reading gem:description prose.
deferred_proposals.note: Surfaced S150 when NCD 200.2 became the third 'no NCD is appropriate' policy and the first that reached the shape by creation rather than retirement. gem:isInEffect is currently doing double duty (currentness AND retirement) and disagrees with itself across the four: 200.2/180.2/240.2.2 true, 280.13 false. No gem:policyStatus property exists; the distinction lives only in prose, so a count by status is a read, not a query, and nothing checks it. Candidate: a gem:policyStatus object property over a controlled-vocabulary family (gem:PolicyStatus), annotated per the gem_llm_annotations.json mirror workflow, with an audit check deriving status from the graph rather than a roster (the nca_uri_derivation model). Scope question for the review: whether 'never determined' is a status or a rule-content fact, and whether retirement is orthogonal to isInEffect rather than encoded in it. Related: the written definition owed for gem:isInEffect (handoff S149 §4 item 11 / S148 §3 B5) -- these two should be decided together. PARTIALLY DECIDED (S156, Tom): the *access* axis is now its own property and is out of this proposal's scope. gem:sourceAvailability -> gem:SourceAvailability { gem:sourceUnobtainable } records whether a document's source rendition is obtainable, which is orthogonal to both gem:isInEffect and gem:nextPlannedStep -- gemi:tn78CIM is in effect, has no work planned, and is paper-only, and the three facts are independent. It was built on this proposal's own recommended shape (property + controlled-vocabulary family + gem_llm_annotations.json mirror + an audit check deriving state from the graph rather than a roster), so it doubles as a worked precedent for the lifecycle axis. WHAT REMAINS UNCHANGED: the four-member lifecycle question (active / retired-in-place / retired-and-removed / never-determined) and gem:isInEffect's double duty over currentness AND retirement. Deliberately NOT folded in: 'unobtainable' is not a lifecycle state, and adding it to a lifecycle vocabulary would have rebuilt the same overload on a new property. One design point worth carrying over: the access vocabulary has ONE member and no affirmative 'available', because absence of the property has to stay meaningful (= unchecked) for the unverified set to be derivable; a lifecycle vocabulary with an explicit 'active' member cannot borrow that trick, which is part of what the review must decide.
deferred_proposals.resolution: Resolved 2026-07-17, Session 159. The lifecycle axis dissolves; no gem:policyStatus property and no gem:PolicyStatus vocabulary are built, and none is needed. The proposal's four candidate members were the shadow of two other things. (1) gem:isInEffect was carrying a second question. Its S45 definition read document-level in one sentence and version-level in another, and gem_reference.md 2k's default row 'Other stub, is_current=false -> planNone/false' -- not the definition -- is what assigned the value; the discriminator across the three retired NCDs turned out to be stub-vs-extracted, not removed-vs-in-place. Tom settled the question at S159: gem:isInEffect is true while the document is still carried by its publisher and false only where GEM has knowledge that the publisher removed it; retirement in place does not remove it and absence of knowledge is not removal. That IS the retired-in-place / retired-and-removed line, drawn as a definition rather than a vocabulary -- and under it 'retired-and-removed' is simply DELETED, so ncd280.13 joins the five _DELETED individuals and the NCD count is 51 active / 0 stubs / 2 retired / 6 deleted (both earlier counts, S150's and S158's, were wrong, for different reasons). (2) 'never-determined' and 'retired-in-place' are not lifecycle at all -- the shared 'no NCD is appropriate; the MACs decide' content is rule content and belongs to deferred_proposals[90] (MAC-discretion coverage polarity), which already carries ncd180.2 and ncd240.2.2 in its also_seen_in and is at five policies against a threshold of three. NCD 200.2 is a sixth instance and is NOT yet listed there (S159 finding). What separates ncd180.2 from ncd200.2 is only whether a prior version carried substantive rules, which becomes derivable the moment version individuals exist. The access axis was already split out at S156 (gem:sourceAvailability) and is untouched. Executed at S159: gem:isInEffect's four annotations rewritten; gem:planNone narrowed to a statement of intent and nothing else (Tom, S159 -- 'planNone only refers to there being no intent to take it further; no other meaning should be inferred'); 2k's default table rebuilt with one road to false; 37 instance values corrected (31 transmittals, 4 NCAs, 2 change requests -- all recording a TARGET's supersession, not their own removal); the planPromote/isInEffect=False sub-section removed as unreachable. Zero of the 103 document-class values needed changing -- they were right all along. See gem_reference.md 2k 'What gem:isInEffect means' (which also closes the written-definition scrap carried since S148 3 B5), SKILL.md Common Failure Modes 'a predicate carries a second question', and the S159 handoff. Successor question -- whether a policy governs a given claim -- is deferred_proposals[98]'s and is not this proposal's.

deferred_proposals.concept_group: Multi-version policy management (rule provenance across versions)
deferred_proposals.example: NCD 240.1's gem:PolicyRule set spans three versions: r1-r9 are V3's own text, r10 carries V2's NETT-participant coverage leg, and r11-r14 carry four V1 factors. All fourteen are indistinguishable in the graph -- each is a gem:PolicyRule with dc:source gemi:ncd240.1 and no marker of which version's text it is. A consumer cannot tell r13 (V1's payment rule, retained because no revision history ever reported its removal) from r1 (V3's approach limitation) without reading gem_rule_categories.md.
deferred_proposals.note: Surfaced S151 when NCD 240.1 became the corpus's first multi-version rule set. Tom's B2' ruling (S151) is deliberate and is the current design: a PolicyRule declares itself by its existence; a later version's revision changes its text and a later version's deletion removes the individual, so no per-rule version stamp is carried. The retention rule (S151) that produced r10-r14 is what makes the gap visible -- retained rules are, by construction, text the current version does not contain, and nothing in the graph says so. Worked examples now exist from this pass and from the cross-version audits. Candidate directions, none evaluated: (a) accept the gap, register is the record; (b) a gem:statedInVersion datatype property on gem:PolicyRule; (c) version individuals as first-class gem:CMSpolicy siblings with gem:supersedes edges, which would also give TN 83's pre-V1 policy state somewhere to live. Note (c) interacts with deferred_proposals[97] (policy status vocabulary) and with the gem:isInEffect double-duty problem. Do not act without a Tom decision on which question the graph should answer: 'what is in force now' (current design) or 'what was in force on date D' (a materially larger model). | S152 second live instance -- NCD 270.1. Two things it adds beyond NCD 240.1's. (1) SECTION-NUMBER HISTORY: 270.1 has been published under three manual coordinates -- Pub. 6 §35-98 (V1), Pub. 6 §35-102 (V2), Pub. 100-3 §270.1 (V3) -- because CMS converted the Coverage Issues Manual into the NCD Manual and renumbered within it. gem:publicationNumber and gem:manualSectionNumber are single-valued current-version facts, so before S152 the graph recorded ZERO prior coordinates corpus-wide and a citation written against an old coordinate resolved to nothing. Tom chose option (c) at S152: a new repeatable gem:priorManualSectionNumber datatype property carrying the full coordinate as the superseded rendition prints it ('Pub. 6 §35-98'). It is deliberately partial -- it makes old-coordinate lookup work and carries no date and no version linkage. Options considered and rejected: (a) prose only (not queryable); (b) multi-valuing gem:manualSectionNumber (destroys 'what is the section now' and dates nothing). Option (d) -- first-class version individuals -- subsumes (c) and remains THIS proposal's open question. If (d) is ever built, (c) is throwaway; Tom accepted that at S152. (2) NO RETAINED RULES: 270.1's retention analysis retained nothing, because both silent drops were restatements or reported changes -- so the corpus now has one multi-version policy with retained rules (240.1) and one without, and neither is distinguishable in the graph from a single-version policy. That is the same gap this proposal names; 270.1 does not widen it, but it does show the gap is not rare. A THIRD sub-question surfaced at 270.1 and is NOT answered: PM B-97-11 suspended the V1 policy's implementation in 12/1997, every version's Revision History still reports the suspension, no entry reports it being lifted, and V2/V3 state substantive coverage rules anyway. Whether the graph should be able to express 'stated but suspended' is a policy-status question that touches deferred_proposals[97] as much as this entry. | S159 ADDITION -- the date axis reached this proposal from the gem:isInEffect side, and it arrives with a decision it did not have before. Four questions from Tom established that 'in effect' takes two arguments, a policy VERSION and a DATE OF SERVICE, and that gem:isInEffect carries neither: the range of dates is a property of the version, not the policy (CMS's own field is named 'Ending Effective Date of this Version' and the Other Versions table tiles one interval per version), and the policy's range is the union of its versions'. GEM holds the interval's OPEN end only -- gem:policyEffectiveDate, 82 uses, whose own description says 'the current VERSION took legal effect' and whose cardinality note says 'one per policy version', so it is a version fact on a policy subject under a policy name -- and has NO property for the closing end. 31 individuals carry a numeric policyVersion > 1, and for every one of them gem:policyEffectiveDate reads as a false statement about the policy. CONSEQUENCE, evidenced: a retired policy still governs claims dated before its retirement, permanently (retirement is prospective; litigation extends the window in which the fact is consulted, not the fact). gemi:ncd180.2 carries exactly ONE rule -- the 2022 'no NCD is appropriate' determination -- and is gem:isInEffect true, so a 2021 enteral-nutrition claim in litigation passes any filter, matches on conceptEnteralNutritionalTherapy, and gets a CONFIDENTLY WRONG answer rather than a missing one; V1's substantive criteria are not in the graph (this policy's own B2: 'change-log only ... not modeled in the graph'). That is worse than NCD 40.2's and NCD 140.1's silent misses, whose registers already say in as many words that 'a 1995-2006 / 1998-2006 date-of-service claim would have' mapped and now cannot. deferred_proposals.example: NCD 160.7.1's r15 denies electrical nerve stimulation treatments furnished by a physician in the office, by a physical therapist or outpatient clinic, under Section 1862(a)(1). Read alone it is a bare setting-and-credential exclusion. Its actual scope is fixed by other rules: r9 establishes that PENS is a DIAGNOSTIC procedure performed only in the physician's office, clinic, or hospital outpatient department, so the denial does not reach the diagnostic service in those same places; r14 establishes the CONTINUING-BASIS phase, after the patient is trained, which is when the denial bites. The physician's office therefore carries gem:exclusivelyCoversInHealthcareSetting on r9 and gem:excludesHealthcareSetting on r15 with no conflict -- and nothing in the graph records WHY. TN 2476's BR 04.21 place-of-service closed list is the likely second instance, and NCD 240.2's r20/r21 (initial coverage limited to 90 days, renewal if medically necessary) is the same shape without settings.
deferred_proposals.note: TOM (S198): 'A denial takes into account the conditions of the denial -- the credentials, the service, the diagnosis, the setting, when the service occurs, and any other stated factors may be conditions on which the denial is determined. Earlier, concurrent, or subsequent statements may also describe a factor that is included in the determination.' And: 'Interpreting rules is not always simple. All of the rules have to be considered, and it's important to evaluate which rules relate to a determination of coverage or denial.' PROBLEM. GEM currently models each gem:PolicyRule as an independent statement carrying its own polarity links. Where one rule supplies a condition that scopes another rule's determination, the relation is invisible: a downstream reader sees r15's two exclusion links and cannot tell that r9 carves the diagnostic service out of them or that r14 fixes the phase. The conditioning is real and stated in the source, but it is stated ACROSS rules rather than inside one. TWO QUESTIONS, both Tom's. (1) SCOPE -- should GEM record the conditioning relation at all, or does it stop at recording each rule faithfully and leave the assembly to the downstream evaluator? GEM extracts and does not evaluate, so the test is whether the conditioning is STATED by the source or ASSEMBLED by a reader, and NCD 160.7.1 sits close to that line: each condition is stated, the linkage between them is not.
